doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Work routine
summary: She works mornings, thinks about lyrics all day and sings through them constantly.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you have a work pattern? I’ve often read, talking about authors and composers, that you have to have a routine, you have to write something every day even if you have no particular impetus or inspiration, you just have to keep writing. Do you find that is true?

Not exactly. There are days when I don’t write. But if I have songs in progress I like to go visit them on any given day and maybe change a thing or two. I’m not super disciplined that way. I start in the morning — if I begin a song in the morning, a lyric, I can work on it into the night but I would never, almost never, start anything at night or in the late afternoon. I like to be hopped up on caffeine and in a certain mental condition to

begin writing a lyric. But then if I go out walking or when I used to have a garden if I’m outside gardening it just — it just, yeah, sort of courses through my mind the whole time. And that’s how it happens. I don’t consider it like a real job, although on any given day I might get up and go okay, I’m going to work on such-and-such today and I’ll just do it all day long. Or if for example Eddie and I are working on the title tune for the Green World album, we’ll call and we’ll talk through something and we’ll figure out a little section and we’ll try out certain things on my voice. Or we’ll work on harmonies. And then he’ll go, “Okay I’m going to program this so I’ll call you back.” And I’ll go okay, I’ll go have a sandwich or talk to my cat or do any other thing. And then it just goes on and off all day. So I wouldn’t say I have a schedule but I don’t let months go by without writing, ever. Like I can’t do that.
Do you walk around your apartment reading your lyrics, trying them out?

Yeah, I do. I sing through them a lot. Sometimes I put on my noise-canceling headphones and I’ll sing through something with one ear slightly off, and that’s what happens when I’m working on an album. I sing through everything constantly until I’m done.
